summary: Los Angeles County lookout on Topanga State Park ridge, built fall 1934 and in service to at least 1969; graffiti-covered concrete base remains, reached by fire road.

facts.design: California Region BC-301 cabin on a 30-foot K-brace steel tower (register says the design appears to be a USFS one)
facts.status_note: Tower removed or demolished after operations ended; a concrete platform, the former foundation, remains and is covered in graffiti

access.note: Reached by fire road from the Stunt Road and Saddle Peak Road junction; sources name different owners (Mountains Restoration Trust vs Los Angeles County)

visit.drive_up: Park off the road at the junction of Stunt Road and Saddle Peak roads
visit.trail_note: The trail is a fire road leading to the site of the lookout

events.note: Constructed in the fall of 1934 by the county (register says Fire Department; Forest Lookouts says Forestry Department)
Register says the tower was in service to at least 1969
islands.com says operations ceased in 1972 and that the tower was later demolished; islands.com gives no demolition date (trail guide says the 1970s; register says unknown)

sources.title: An Abandoned Fire Lookout High Above A Los Angeles Canyon Is A Colorful Graffiti Gallery With Ocean Views

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives removal as unknown and says the tower was in service to at least 1969. The trail guide says it was removed in the 1970s. Islands.com says operations ceased in 1972 and the tower was demolished. The story reports all three.
The register names the Los Angeles County Fire Department; the Forest Lookouts page names the county's forestry department for the 1934 construction.
The trail guide says the Mountains Restoration Trust owns the site. Islands.com says Los Angeles County owns it. The sources do not reconcile this.

notes_for_editor: Built date, design and the graffiti-covered base are well sourced. Removal date and owner conflict across sources. The brief's access 'unknown' is now 'public' based on the trail guide and islands.com. No staffing names or fires are sourced, so none are given. Height 9.1 m is the register's 30 feet converted; it describes the tower only. The removal year 1972 was dropped from the events list: islands.com gives 1972 as the end of operations, not a demolition date.
